Appendix C Blow up of Christoffel symbols

In Theorems 5.4 and 5.5 (see, in particular, (5.16) and (5.18)), we have seen that the scalar field fails to be in Wl​o​c1,2W^{1,2}_{loc} near every point of 𝒞​ℋ1+\mathcal{C}\mathcal{H}^{+}_{1} in the C0C^{0} extension constructed in Theorems 5.1 and 5.5, respectively, provided that (5.15) holds on ℋ1+\mathcal{H}^{+}_{1}. In this section of the appendix, we investigate in more detail the geometry near 𝒞​ℋ1+\mathcal{C}\mathcal{H}^{+}_{1} under the same assumptions, and show that certain Christoffel symbols blow up in any Ll​o​cpL^{p}_{loc} for p>1p>1. More precisely, our goal is to prove the following result:

Proposition C.1.

Let (u,V)(u,V) be the null coordinates constructed in Theorem 5.5, with respect to which the solution extends continuously to 𝒞​ℋ1+∖{p𝒞​ℋ1+}\mathcal{C}\mathcal{H}^{+}_{1}\setminus\{p_{\mathcal{C}\mathcal{H}^{+}_{1}}\}. If the lower bound (5.15) holds on ℋ1+\mathcal{H}^{+}_{1}, then for every u∈(−∞,u𝒞​ℋ1+)u\in(-\infty,u_{\mathcal{C}\mathcal{H}^{+}_{1}}) and p>1p>1, we have

∫01|(σ𝕊2−1)A​B​ΓA​Bu|p​Ω2​(u,V)​𝑑V=∞.\int_{0}^{1}|(\sigma_{\mathbb{S}^{2}}^{-1})^{AB}\Gamma^{u}_{AB}|^{p}\Omega^{2}(u,V)\,dV=\infty. (C.1)

Moreover, we have supV∈[0,1)|(σ𝕊2−1)A​B​ΓA​Bu|(V)=∞\sup_{V\in[0,1)}|(\sigma_{\mathbb{S}^{2}}^{-1})^{AB}\Gamma^{u}_{AB}|(V)=\infty.

Recall that, in any null coordinates, we have ΓA​Bu=2​Ω−2​r​∂Vr​(σ𝕊2)A​B\Gamma^{u}_{AB}=2\Omega^{-2}r\partial_{V}r(\sigma_{\mathbb{S}^{2}})_{AB}. In view of continuous extendibility of rr, the blow up of the supremum already follows from (5.17) and (5.19). In what follows, we exploit further the Raychaudhuri equation, (5.16) and bounds proved in Section 10 to upgrade this blow-up statement.

Proof.

Fix p∈(1,∞)p\in(1,\infty). We begin with a few reductions. First, by the above formula for ΓA​Bu\Gamma^{u}_{AB}, it suffices to show that

∫01(−∂VrΩ2)p​Ω2​(u,V)​𝑑V=∞ for every ​u∈(−∞,u𝒞​ℋ1+).\int_{0}^{1}\left(-\frac{\partial_{V}r}{\Omega^{2}}\right)^{p}\Omega^{2}(u,V)\,dV=\infty\quad\hbox{ for every }u\in(-\infty,u_{\mathcal{C}\mathcal{H}^{+}_{1}}). (C.2)

In view of the bounds C−1≤Ω2​(u,V)≤CC^{-1}\leq\Omega^{2}(u,V)\leq C and |∂u(r​∂Vr)|​(u,V)≤C|\partial_{u}(r\partial_{V}r)|(u,V)\leq C, which hold in any rectangle ℛ={(u,V):u0≤u≤u1, 0≤V<1}\mathcal{R}=\{(u,V):u_{0}\leq u\leq u_{1},\,0\leq V<1\} for some 0<C<∞0<C<\infty (see (10.13) in the proof of Lemma 10.5), it suffices to prove (C.2) under the additional assumption that uu lies in the perturbative region, i.e., u<usu<u_{s} where usu_{s} is as in Theorem 5.1. Furthermore, note that both ∂VrΩ2\frac{\partial_{V}r}{\Omega^{2}} and Ω2​d​V\Omega^{2}\,dV on the LHS of (C.2) are invariant under any change of the null coordinate VV. Hence, using the (u,v)(u,v) coordinates in Theorem 5.1, we see that it suffices to prove

∫1∞(−∂vrΩ2)p​Ω2​(u,v)​𝑑v=∞ for every ​u∈(−∞,us),\int_{1}^{\infty}\left(-\frac{\partial_{v}r}{\Omega^{2}}\right)^{p}\Omega^{2}(u,v)\,dv=\infty\quad\hbox{ for every }u\in(-\infty,u_{s}), (C.3)

where Ω2\Omega^{2} is now defined with respect to the (u,v)(u,v) coordinates.

In the remainder of the proof, we fix a value of u<usu<u_{s} and omit the dependence of constants on uu. Let η>0\eta>0 be a parameter to be fixed later (and we allow the constants CC below to depend on η\eta). By the integrated blow up statement (5.16), we may find a sequence vk∈ℕ∩[2,∞)v_{k}\in\mathbb{N}\cap[2,\infty) such that vkv_{k} increases to ∞\infty and

∫vk−1vklog+α0⁡(1Ω)​(∂vϕ)2​(u,v)​𝑑v≥e−η​vk.\int_{v_{k}-1}^{v_{k}}\log_{+}^{\alpha_{0}}(\frac{1}{\Omega})(\partial_{v}\phi)^{2}(u,v)\,dv\geq e^{-\eta v_{k}}. (C.4)

Next, by the Raychaudhuri equation (2.4), for any v≥vkv\geq v_{k} we have

−∂vrΩ2​(u,v)≥∫vk−1vkrΩ2​(∂vϕ)2​(u,v′)​d​v′−∂vrΩ2​(u,vk−1).-\frac{\partial_{v}r}{\Omega^{2}}(u,v)\geq\int_{v_{k}-1}^{v_{k}}\frac{r}{\Omega^{2}}(\partial_{v}\phi)^{2}(u,v^{\prime})\,dv^{\prime}-\frac{\partial_{v}r}{\Omega^{2}}(u,v_{k}-1).

By (5.17), we may assume that the last term on the right-hand side is nonnegative (and thus can be dropped) by taking v1v_{1} sufficiently large. To estimate the first term, we use (C.4) and also recall from Theorem 5.1 (in particular, the bounds for r−rR​Nr-r_{RN} and log⁡Ω−log⁡ΩR​N\log\Omega-\log\Omega_{RN}) that C−1≤r≤CC^{-1}\leq r\leq C and C−1​e−κ−​v≤Ω≤C​e−κ−​vC^{-1}e^{-\kappa_{-}v}\leq\Omega\leq Ce^{-\kappa_{-}v}. Hence,

−∂vrΩ2​(u,v)≥C−1​e(2​κ−−η)​vk​vk−α0 for every ​v≥vk.-\frac{\partial_{v}r}{\Omega^{2}}(u,v)\geq C^{-1}e^{(2\kappa_{-}-\eta)v_{k}}v_{k}^{-\alpha_{0}}\quad\hbox{ for every }v\geq v_{k}.

It follows that

∫1∞(−∂vrΩ2)p​Ω2​(u,v)​𝑑v≥∑k=1∞∫vkvk+1(−∂vrΩ2)p​Ω2​(u,v)​𝑑v≥C−1​∑k=1∞e2​(p−1)​κ−​vk−p​η​vk​vk−p​α0.\displaystyle\int_{1}^{\infty}\left(-\frac{\partial_{v}r}{\Omega^{2}}\right)^{p}\Omega^{2}(u,v)\,dv\geq\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\int_{v_{k}}^{v_{k}+1}\left(-\frac{\partial_{v}r}{\Omega^{2}}\right)^{p}\Omega^{2}(u,v)\,dv\geq C^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}e^{2(p-1)\kappa_{-}v_{k}-p\eta v_{k}}v_{k}^{-p\alpha_{0}}.

Since p>1p>1, choosing η>0\eta>0 sufficiently small ensures that each summand on the right-hand side is uniformly bounded from below, which in turn makes the sum infinite as desired. ∎

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research.
